Ui.Script:
-- The reference's own body, captured before we shadow the name. Nil on a machine with no -- client data (nothing was sourced) — which must be LOUD at the call, not a quiet no-op: -- a bag hover that silently does nothing is precisely the failure mode that let Bagnon -- ship "working" through four green survey columns. local refItemButtonOnEnter = ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter
function ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter(button) if not button then button = this end if not button then return end
-- benilla's keyring is a CONTAINER (0765), so the reference's inventory-slot detour is -- both unavailable and wrong here; this is the same pair of calls its general path -- makes for every other bag, which is all a keyring slot ever needed. if button:GetParent():GetID() == KEYRING_CONTAINER then if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(KEYRING_CONTAINER, button:GetID()) ResetCursor() return end
if not refItemButtonOnEnter then message("benilla: Interface\\FrameXML\\ContainerFrame.lua was not sourced from the " .. "game data, so bag-slot tooltips cannot work. Check the client data path.") return end refItemButtonOnEnter(button) end
-- ══ The three bag verbs benilla answers differently (decisions 0561 + 1751) ═════════ -- -- `CloseAllBags`, `OpenBackpack` and `CloseBackpack` all exist in the sourced -- `ContainerFrame.lua` too, and benilla's differ for one reason, not three: **0561, the -- director's call that a window which opens your bags opens EVERY equipped bag**, not just -- the backpack. The vendor/bank/mail/trade windows call `OpenBackpack` from their OnShow so -- your bags come up with them and you can sell or deposit from one; the reference's own -- body touches bag 0 alone. `CloseBackpack` is its inverse and has to match it, and -- `CloseAllBags` is the same family's unconditional form. -- -- **The `Benilla*` names, and the publish under them, are load ORDER** (1751). Order -- decides every collision and the manifest is the order: this file loads after the -- reference's `ContainerFrame.xml`, so the three publishes at the foot are the ones that -- stand. The bodies lived in our UIParent.lua counterpart until 1988 retired it — a -- harness with no bag stack now meets the loader's stand-ins for the three names -- (`test_ui::UIPARENT_STAND_INS`), not a nil. -- -- What CHANGED with the swap is only the plumbing: these used to walk five benilla windows -- by name and stash `wasOpen` on each frame. The windows are the reference's recycled -- `ContainerFrame1..12` now — frame N is a different bag every time it opens — so the -- was-open memory is keyed by BAG ID, and every open and close goes through the -- reference's own `OpenBag`/`CloseBag`/`IsBagOpen` rather than a raw Show/Hide. That buys -- the reference's own guards for free (OpenBag's CanOpenPanels + NotWhileDeadError, -- ToggleBag's `size > 0`) and means an addon replacing those verbs is honoured here too. BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN = {}
-- The UNCONDITIONAL close, called by ShowUIPanel's native-center branch above: a centre -- frame takes the whole screen, so nothing is being "restored afterwards" the way a vendor -- window restores the bags it opened, and the was-open memory is deliberately ignored. -- Range 0..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES rather than the old five names — the reference's own -- CloseAllBags covers the bank bags too (l.702-707), and now so does this. function BenillaCloseAllBags() for bagId = 0, (NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES or -1) do CloseBag(bagId) end end
-- OpenBackpack — 0561's all-bags form. A bag already open is REMEMBERED and left alone, so -- the paired CloseBackpack does not close a window the player opened themselves; that -- memory is the reference's own `backpackWasOpen`, one entry per bag instead of one flag. function BenillaOpenBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do -- The backpack always exists; an equipped-bag window only when a bag is in the -- slot — `OpenBag` makes the same test itself, but the memory has to agree with it. if bagId == 0 or GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0 then if IsBagOpen(bagId) then BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = 1 else BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = nil OpenBag(bagId) end end end end
function BenillaCloseBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do if not BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] then CloseBag(bagId) end end end
-- The publish — after the reference's container file, so these are the definitions that -- stand (the stock `ShowUIPanel` calls `CloseAllBags` and the vendor's OnShow -- `OpenBackpack`, and they reach 0561's bodies). OpenBackpack = BenillaOpenBackpack CloseBackpack = BenillaCloseBackpack CloseAllBags = BenillaCloseAllBags
